title: Enums Lacking Non-Exhaustive Annotation
pattern: Exposing a public `enum` in a library API that is intended to grow during future feature migrations, without annotating it with the `#[non_exhaustive]` attribute.
why_bad: When the library author adds a new variant (e.g., `Failed`) in a minor version v1.1.0 update, all downstream users' code containing `match` statements over this enum will immediately fail to compile because their matches are no longer exhaustive, breaking backwards compatibility [536].
detection: A public `enum` lacking `#[non_exhaustive]` that is matched on by external crates, combined with minor version additions of new variants.
counterexample: Valid for stable, closed enums that are mathematically guaranteed to never acquire new variants (e.g., `enum Direction { North, South, East, West }`).
fix:
Mark all public enums that are subject to future migration or expansion as `#[non_exhaustive]` [536].
```rust
#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum TaskStatus {
    Pending,
    Running,
    Completed,
    Failed, // Safe addition
}
```
